claims.claim: S3 Options and emitters. Options are single-word keys grouped by entity noun, `on` reserved for hooks; a stateful entity owns an Emitter by composition with the seven-step pattern and a focused event map of present-tense verbs or nouns, no `status` event, errors typed `unknown`.

Then walked the seven-step pattern for each stateful entity: CompilerEventMap/MaterializerEventMap/UpstreamEventMap are declared in types.ts (step 1); every options bag carries `readonly on?: EmitterHooks<…>` and `readonly error?: EmitterErrorHandler` (step 2); every interface carries `readonly emitter: EmitterInterface<…>` (step 3); each class stores `readonly #emitter: Emitter<…>` and exposes `get emitter()` — src/core/Compiler.ts:83/115, src/server/Materializer.ts:130/206, src/server/Upstream.ts:176 (step 4); each constructor threads both hooks and the error handler into one `new Emitter({…})` — src/core/Compiler.ts:108-111, src/server/Materializer.ts:172-175 (step 5); every emit is a direct `this.#emitter.emit(…)` with no guarded #notify — src/core/Compiler.ts:154-155/199/220, src/server/Materializer.ts:1001/1052/1186, src/server/Upstream.ts:422/451/465 (step 6); and `this.#emitter.destroy()` is the last statement of each destroy() — src/core/Compiler.ts:221, src/server/Upstream.ts:354 (step 7). No class inherits from Emitter, writes delegation boilerplate, or uses Omit on it. Every event name is a single present-tense verb or noun (compile, audit, block, error, destroy / write, remove, finish, error, destroy / release, mirror, file, error, destroy), no map publishes a `status` event, every map holds five events, and every `error` tuple is typed `readonly [error: unknown]`.

claims.claim: S4 Design laws. State is derived rather than stored twice; literal unions represent real domain states only; no compatibility shim; mechanism not product policy; no polling architecture; the public API is minimal and every intentional capability is exposed.
